# Authoring & maintaining the `og-preview` skill

Agent guide for working **inside this skill repository**. Read it before editing `SKILL.md`, the README,
or any plugin manifest.

> Naming (Russian): the adjective for "agent / agentic" is **«агентный»**, never «агентский».

## Repository layout

This skill is packaged for **Claude Code**, **Cursor**, and **OpenAI Codex** (and installs as a plain
skill folder for Kimi Code CLI and others).

```
og-preview/
├─ .claude-plugin/
│  └─ plugin.json        # Claude Code plugin manifest
├─ .cursor-plugin/
│  └─ plugin.json        # Cursor plugin manifest
├─ .codex-plugin/
│  └─ plugin.json        # Codex plugin manifest (interface block + skills: "./")
├─ scripts/
│  └─ og_preview.py      # stdlib-only checker + HTML report renderer
├─ references/
│  ├─ index.md           # summary table + shared baseline + crawler UAs
│  └─ platforms/         # one file per platform - edit only what changes
│     ├─ telegram.md     ├─ x.md            ├─ facebook.md
│     ├─ discord.md      ├─ slack.md        ├─ whatsapp.md
│     └─ linkedin.md     ├─ reddit.md       └─ imessage.md
├─ examples/
│  ├─ neuraldeep.ru.html        # captured page fixture
│  ├─ neuraldeep-preview.html   # rendered report (reference output)
│  └─ neuraldeep-report.json    # machine-readable findings
├─ SKILL.md              # CANONICAL skill: YAML frontmatter + instructions (repo root)
├─ README.md             # human overview
├─ AGENTS.md             # this file
└─ LICENSE
```

## Golden rule: a change anywhere must be synced across the whole skill

- `SKILL.md` at the repo root is **canonical**; `scripts/` and `references/` live next to it and are
  referenced by relative path.
- `version` must be identical in `SKILL.md` frontmatter, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`,
  `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`.
- `description` must stay consistent across all manifests (plus `interface.shortDescription` in Codex).
- The `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` must **not** contain a `category` key - the manifest schema rejects it.
- Every release must be mirrored into the `rpa-skills` catalog (both `marketplace.json` files, README
  table when the description changed, catalog `metadata.version` bump).

## Code

`scripts/og_preview.py` is **standard library only** - no pip installs, the skill must work on a bare
Python 3. Keep it that way. When a platform rule changes, update the checker (`check_common`,
truncation budgets in `render_report`), the platform's file in `references/platforms/<name>.md` and
the summary row in `references/index.md` in the same commit. Regenerate `examples/neuraldeep-preview.html`
when rendering or findings change.

## Commit checklist

- [ ] `SKILL.md` edited where needed.
- [ ] `version` bumped and identical in all four manifests.
- [ ] `description` consistent across manifests.
- [ ] README updated.
- [ ] Release mirrored into `rpa-skills` (both manifests, README row, `metadata.version` bump).
- [ ] `python3 scripts/og_preview.py <fixture>` still produces a report.
- [ ] Conventional commit, e.g. `feat(og-preview): …` / `fix(og-preview): …`.

# OG preview

## When this skill applies

The user wants to see how a page's link preview (Open Graph card, Twitter card,
Telegram/Discord/Slack unfurl) will look, or to validate social meta tags -
especially on localhost or a file, where public validators cannot reach.

## Workflow

1. **Run the checker.** Pick the invocation that matches what the user gave:

   ```bash
   # live page, local dev server included
   python3 scripts/og_preview.py http://localhost:3000/blog/post

   # static HTML file; --base makes relative og:image resolvable
   python3 scripts/og_preview.py dist/index.html --base https://example.com/
   ```

   Output: `og-preview.html` (report) in the current directory. Add
   `--json report.json` for machine-readable findings when the fix loop is
   automated. Exit code is 1 when errors are found, 0 otherwise - usable in CI.

2. **Read the findings table first.** Errors (missing `og:title`/`og:image`,
   relative or http image URLs, unreachable image) block correct rendering on
   real platforms; warnings are truncation and size-degradation risks. The
   rules live split by platform under `references/` - consult
   `references/index.md` for the summary table, then open only the files of
   the platforms that flagged findings (`references/platforms/<name>.md`)
   instead of loading every rule.

3. **Show the report.** Open `og-preview.html` for the user (a local preview
   server or the browser tool) so they can compare the nine platform mocks.
   The mocks apply per-platform truncation budgets; they approximate layout,
   not pixel-exact rendering.

4. **Fix and re-run.** Patch the page's `<head>` and re-run until zero errors.
   Typical minimal fix set: `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:site_name`,
   `og:type`, `og:url`, absolute `https://` `og:image` 1200x630 with
   `og:image:width`/`height`/`alt`, `twitter:card=summary_large_image`,
   `theme-color` for Discord/Slack accents.

## Notes

- The only network access is fetching the page itself and its `og:image` for a
  dimension check (`--no-fetch` disables the image fetch). No external
  validators or preview APIs are used - safe for intranet and offline work.
- Mocks cannot reproduce real crawler caches. Remind the user that after
  deploying, Telegram/Facebook cache the first scrape: a changed card needs a
  fresh URL or the platform's re-scrape tool.

# og-preview

Test Open Graph, Twitter Card and social-link meta tags **fully offline**. Give
it a URL - `http://localhost:3000` works - or a plain HTML file, and it renders
a self-contained `og-preview.html` report:

- mocked link-preview cards for **Telegram, X/Twitter, Facebook, Discord,
  Slack, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, Reddit and iMessage**, each applying that
  platform's truncation and layout rules;
- a findings table of rule violations (missing tags, relative or `http://`
  images, localhost-only image URLs, wrong image dimensions, truncation risk);
- a full dump of every meta tag found.

No third-party validators, no external API - a single Python script on the
standard library. The only network calls are fetching the page itself (if you
passed a URL) and its `og:image` for a size check (`--no-fetch` skips it).

## Usage

```bash
python3 scripts/og_preview.py http://localhost:3000/blog/post
python3 scripts/og_preview.py https://example.com/page
python3 scripts/og_preview.py dist/index.html --base https://example.com/
python3 scripts/og_preview.py page.html --json report.json --out preview.html
```

Exit code is `1` when errors are found, `0` otherwise - works as a CI gate.

## Example report

Rendered for [neuraldeep.ru](examples/neuraldeep.ru.html) - nine platform
mocks plus the findings and tag tables:

![OG preview report for neuraldeep.ru](examples/neuraldeep-preview.png)

The same report as HTML: [examples/neuraldeep-preview.html](examples/neuraldeep-preview.html)
(machine-readable findings: [neuraldeep-report.json](examples/neuraldeep-report.json)).

## When to use it

- previewing social cards before deploying a page;
- testing OG tags on a local dev server where public debuggers (Facebook
  Sharing Debugger, LinkedIn Post Inspector) cannot reach;
- a repeatable, scriptable check of meta markup in CI.

For the per-platform rules the checker enforces, see
[references/index.md](references/index.md) - a summary table linking to one
file per platform. A worked example (captured page + rendered report) lives in
[examples/](examples/).

## Install

The repo root is the skill folder: copy or symlink it into your agent's skills
directory (`~/.claude/skills/og-preview`, `~/.cursor/skills/og-preview`,
`~/.agents/skills/og-preview`).

Part of the **[rpa-skills](https://github.com/EvilFreelancer/rpa-skills)**
marketplace - the recommended way to install:

```bash
# Claude Code
/plugin marketplace add EvilFreelancer/rpa-skills
/plugin install og-preview@rpa-skills

# Codex
codex plugin marketplace add EvilFreelancer/rpa-skills

# any agent with a skills folder
git clone https://github.com/EvilFreelancer/og-preview ~/.agents/skills/og-preview
```

## Source & attribution

Written for the rpa-skills collection. Rules compiled from the
[Open Graph protocol](https://ogp.me/) spec and platform crawler
documentation. MIT licensed.

# Link-preview rules - index

Load only the file for the platform you are fixing or checking - do not read
the whole set. Each file lists what that platform's crawler reads, its layout,
its text budgets and its image limits.

## Shared baseline (applies everywhere)

- Crawlers read `og:*` first. The four required properties: `og:title`,
  `og:type`, `og:image`, `og:url`. Strongly recommended: `og:description`,
  `og:site_name`.
- `og:image` MUST be an absolute `https://` URL. Relative paths, `data:` URIs
  and localhost/private hosts are unusable by real crawlers.
- Recommended image: **1200x630** (1.91:1), JPEG/PNG/WebP, under ~5 MB. Under
  600px wide many platforms degrade to a small thumbnail.
- `og:image:width`/`height`/`alt` structured properties apply to the nearest
  preceding `og:image`; several `og:image` tags are allowed, first wins.
- `<title>` and `<meta name="description">` are the universal fallback - but
  NOT guaranteed on LinkedIn.
- `og:url` is the canonical URL; without it crawlers use the requested URL and
  shares of URL variants split.
- Most platforms cache the first scrape hard: a changed card needs a fresh URL
  or the platform's re-scrape tool.

## Per-platform files

| Platform | File | Reads | Card style | Title budget | Description budget | Image minimum |
|----------|------|-------|------------|--------------|--------------------|---------------|
| Telegram | [platforms/telegram.md](platforms/telegram.md) | OG + title fallback | medium card in message | ~65 | ~200 (3 lines) | ~160px wide or no preview |
| X / Twitter | [platforms/x.md](platforms/x.md) | twitter:* then og:* | summary / summary_large_image | ~70 | ~200 | 300x157 large card |
| Facebook / Messenger | [platforms/facebook.md](platforms/facebook.md) | OG | large card | ~88 | ~200 | 200x200 (1200x630 rec.) |
| Discord | [platforms/discord.md](platforms/discord.md) | OG + twitter:card + theme-color | embed with accent bar | - | ~256 | per card type |
| Slack | [platforms/slack.md](platforms/slack.md) | oEmbed > twitter > OG | unfurl with accent bar | - | - | per card type |
| WhatsApp | [platforms/whatsapp.md](platforms/whatsapp.md) | OG only | rounded card | ~2 lines | domain only | re-hosted, center-safe |
| LinkedIn | [platforms/linkedin.md](platforms/linkedin.md) | OG, poor fallbacks | large card | - | ~150 | 1200x627 rec. |
| Reddit | [platforms/reddit.md](platforms/reddit.md) | OG | image + title + domain | - | none | any landscape |
| iMessage | [platforms/imessage.md](platforms/imessage.md) | OG + apple-touch-icon | card | - | none | - |

## Crawler user-agents (for server-side testing)

- Facebook/Meta: `facebookexternalhit/1.1`, `Facebot`
- X/Twitter: `Twitterbot/1.0`
- Telegram: `TelegramBot (like TwitterBot)`
- Slack: `Slackbot-LinkExpanding`
- Discord: `Discordbot/2.0`
- WhatsApp: `WhatsApp/2.x`
- LinkedIn: `LinkedInBot/1.0`
- Pinterest: `Pinterest/0.2`
- Reddit: `redditbot/1.0`

The script sends a facebookexternalhit-compatible UA to approximate the worst
case. A page that varies HTML per UA should still emit complete OG tags for
every UA above.

# Discord

## What the crawler reads

- Open Graph `og:*` plus `twitter:card` for layout selection, and
  `<meta name="theme-color" content="#RRGGBB">` for the embed's left border.
- Crawler UA: `Discordbot/2.0`.

## Card layout

Chat embed: colored accent bar on the left, site name line (og:site_name),
title link, description, then the image - wide under `summary_large_image`,
small right-side thumbnail under `summary`.

## Budgets and limits

- Description: ~256 chars.
- Site name comes from `og:site_name`; falls back to domain.
- `theme-color` accent is a nice touch unique to Discord/Slack embeds.

## Gotchas

- oEmbed/JSON endpoints on the page can override all meta-derived fields.
- Image must be a fetchable absolute URL; Discord re-proxies media.

# Facebook / Messenger

## What the crawler reads

- Open Graph `og:*` via the `facebookexternalhit/1.1` / `Facebot` crawler.
- Reference scraper: Meta's Sharing Debugger (developers.facebook.com/tools/debug).

## Card layout

Large card: wide image on top, domain, title, description below (description
often hidden in the mobile feed layout).

## Budgets and limits

- Large card requires >=200x200; >=600x315 for the large layout;
  1200x630 recommended, <=8 MB.
- Title: ~88 chars.
- Description: ~200 chars, and frequently not displayed at all on mobile.

## Gotchas

- Previews are cached hard - a changed `og:image` or title needs a re-scrape
  via the Sharing Debugger.
- `fb:app_id` is optional, only needed for Insights.

# iMessage / Apple Messages

## What the crawler reads

- Open Graph `og:*`, with `<link rel="apple-touch-icon">` as an image
  fallback. Apple's crawler fetches the page like a normal browser.

## Card layout

Bubble preview: image (wide or square), title, domain. No description.

## Budgets and limits

- Title and domain only - keep the title self-sufficient.
- Square images are accepted better here than on most platforms.

## Gotchas

- Rich previews need the page reachable over https.
- If nothing renders, check that the image is a real raster (PNG/JPEG),
  not SVG.

# LinkedIn

## What the crawler reads

- Open Graph `og:*` specifically: `og:title`, `og:image`, `og:description`,
  `og:url`. The crawler is poor at falling back to `<title>` - emit real OG
  tags. Crawler UA: `LinkedInBot/1.0`.

## Card layout

Post preview: wide image, title, domain.

## Budgets and limits

- Image: 1200x627 recommended.
- Description: cut around ~140-150 chars.
- Title: ~100 chars.

## Gotchas

- Official debugger: LinkedIn Post Inspector.
- First scrape is cached; the Inspector forces a refresh.

# Reddit

## What the crawler reads

- Open Graph `og:*` for link posts. Crawler UA: `redditbot/1.0`.

## Card layout

Link post card: image, title, domain. No description is shown.

## Budgets and limits

- Any reasonable landscape image works; 1.91:1 is safe.
- Title is the only text besides the domain - make it self-sufficient.

## Gotchas

- Subreddit link-flair and thumbnail rules can override the visual in some
  listing views, but the OG card is what a post shows.

# Slack

## What the crawler reads

- Priority order: oEmbed, then `twitter:*` card tags, then `og:*`.
- Crawler UA: `Slackbot-LinkExpanding`.

## Card layout

Unfurl under the message: accent bar on the left (from `theme-color`),
site name, bold title, description, image - wide under
`summary_large_image`, ~75px thumbnail otherwise.

## Budgets and limits

- Same truncation character as Discord (~250 chars of description).
- `twitter:card=summary_large_image` is the lever for the wide image.

## Gotchas

- Respects robots.txt; image URL must be reachable without auth.
- Slack caches unfurls per workspace; `chat.unfurl` in its API is for apps,
  not for fixing stale previews.

# Telegram ## What the crawler reads - Open Graph `og:*`, falling back to `` and `<meta name="description">`. - If `og:image` is missing, Telegram may pick an arbitrary `<img>` from the page. - Crawler UA: `TelegramBot (like TwitterBot)`. ## Card layout Inline preview under/inside the message: site name (og:site_name or domain), bold title, description lines, medium-width image. ## Budgets and limits - Title: ~65 chars safe, then cut. - Description: ~3 lines, ~200 chars safe. - Image under ~160px wide often yields NO preview at all. - Image aspect: landscape preferred; square renders but crops less nicely. ## Gotchas - Preview is generated server-side once per URL and cached aggressively. Changed tags need a new URL (any query param) or the WebPageBot (@WebpageBot) refresh. - Instant View (`tg:iv_*` / `og:` extra fields) is a separate mechanism, not needed for a normal link card.

# WhatsApp

## What the crawler reads

- Open Graph `og:*` only. Crawler UA: `WhatsApp/2.x`.

## Card layout

Rounded card inside the message: image on top (or small thumb), title
(~2 lines), domain at the bottom. Description is rarely shown.

## Budgets and limits

- Title: ~2 rendered lines (~65 chars safe).
- No reliable description display - keep meaning in the title and image.

## Gotchas

- The image is downloaded and re-hosted; large images get cropped toward
  square-ish aspect in practice - keep important content centered.
- Requires absolute https image URL like everyone else.

# X / Twitter

## What the crawler reads

- `twitter:*` tags first, then falls back to `og:*`.
- `twitter:card` selects the layout; without it X renders `summary`.
- Crawler UA: `Twitterbot/1.0`.

## Card types

- `summary` - small square thumbnail beside text.
- `summary_large_image` - big 1.91:1 card, image needs >=300x157,
  recommended 1200x628, <=5 MB.
- `player`, `app` - special cases (video iframe / app store card), rare.

## Budgets and limits

- Title: ~70 chars before truncation.
- Description: ~200 chars; may be omitted entirely in some clients.
- `twitter:site` / `twitter:creator` (`@handle`) - optional attribution.
- `twitter:image` may differ from `og:image`; same absolute-https rule applies.

## Gotchas

- The old Card Validator tool was removed. To see a real render, compose a
  draft tweet with the URL (the card appears in the composer) or rely on this
  skill's mock.
- Robots.txt blocks on `Twitterbot` kill the card silently.
